candidates.statement: Checkout 502s originate downstream: gateway POST /v1/checkout fails because order returns 502, and order's payment call returns 503 (payment /v1/authorizations). Inventory reservation succeeds (200). The failing hop is order->payment, producing the gateway 502s.
candidates.uncertainty: No payment-side logs/metrics admitted; whether payment 503 stems from its own fault or resource exhaustion is unconfirmed.

report.explanation: Traces show gateway /v1/checkout 502s caused by order returning 502, which in turn fails on payment /v1/authorizations 503; inventory/redis reservations succeed. Metrics confirm ~10.7 502s on /v1/checkout in 60s. Root cause is bounded to the order->payment hop, but payment-side evidence is absent, so cause is not fully pinned.
missing_evidence: Payment service logs/metrics for /v1/authorizations 503s to confirm the failing hop's cause
Order service logs to confirm it propagates payment 503 as 502 to gateway
